reason: While the text contains some instances of leaders and people working together (notably the battle with Amalek where Joshua leads fighters while Moses/Aaron/Hur support, and Jethro's judicial reform establishing shared leadership), the dominant pattern throughout this narrative is one of hierarchical command with frequent resistance. The people repeatedly murmur and complain against Moses and Aaron (וַיִּלֹּ֧נוּ הָעָ֛ם עַל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה - "the people complained against Moses"), question God's provision, and express doubt. The leaders generally issue directives that the people follow reluctantly or under duress rather than as willing collaborators. True collaboration implies mutual cooperation and shared decision-making, which is not the dominant characteristic of their relationship in this text.
